basis: RSL class I bHLH that specifies epidermal cells bulging out of the epidermal plane into rhizoids, mucilage papillae and gemmae (Proust et al. 2016 Curr Biol)
validation: Mprsl1 mutants lack rhizoids, mucilage papillae and gemmae, rescued by MpRSL1 cDNA (Fig 1-2); transcript in rhizoids and, by laser-capture single-cell RT-PCR, in gemma-cup epidermal cells that form papillae and gemmae (Fig 3, S3)

basis: RSL class I bHLH required for mucilage papilla development (Proust et al. 2016 Curr Biol)
validation: Mprsl1 mutants lack mucilage papillae, rescued by MpRSL1 cDNA; laser-capture single-cell RT-PCR detects it in gemma-cup cells forming papillae (Fig 3, S3)

basis: RSL class I bHLH required for gemma development from gemma-cup epidermal cells (Proust et al. 2016 Curr Biol)
validation: Mprsl1 mutants lack gemmae, rescued by MpRSL1 cDNA; laser-capture single-cell RT-PCR detects it in gemma-cup cells forming gemmae (Fig 3, S3)

basis: AP2/ERF master regulator that initiates gemma initials, upstream of GCAM1 (Takahashi et al. 2026 Curr Biol)
validation: proMpGMFR:H2B-3xCitrine in the meristem, gemma-cup floor cells and the earliest gemma stages (Fig 2); gmfr mutants and amiRNA lines lack gemmae and gemma cups; inducible GMFR produces gemma initials at the meristem

basis: R2R3-MYB effector of gemma initiation downstream of GMFR (Takahashi et al. 2026 Curr Biol)
validation: expressed in early gemma development after MpGMFR; GCAM1 overexpression partly restores gemma and gemma-cup formation in gmfr

basis: RopGEF needed for the first elongation and asymmetric division of gemma initials (Hiwatashi et al. 2019 Curr Biol)
validation: karappo mutants form no gemma initials on the gemma-cup floor; complemented; no cell-specific reporter reported in the abstract

basis: ALOG protein that specifies ventral scale identity by repressing cell division and chloroplast development (Naramoto et al. 2019 PLoS Biol)
validation: proMpLOS1:GUS in ventral scales; functional eGFP-MpLOS1 protein in ventral scales and the cells at their base, absent from the apical meristem; los1 mutants replace scales with green, misspecified outgrowths

basis: IPyA-pathway auxin biosynthesis gene marking the apical stem cell zone; two independent studies agree (Spencer et al. 2024 Development; Hirakawa et al. 2020 Curr Biol; Eklund et al. 2015 Plant Cell)
validation: proMpYUC2:VENUS-NLS high in the stem cell niche of the mature meristem (Spencer 2024); MpYUC2 marks the undifferentiated cells that accumulate after CLE2 treatment (Hirakawa 2020)

basis: CLAVATA1 receptor mediating CLE2 control of stem cell number in the apical notch (Hirakawa et al. 2020 Curr Biol)
validation: expressed broadly in the central meristem, including the MpYUC2 domain; Mpclv1 mutants are insensitive to MpCLE2 peptide

basis: NAC TF downstream of CLE signaling that controls stem cell behavior in the notch (Takahashi et al. 2023 Curr Biol)
validation: reporter strong at the stem cell zone periphery with periclinal divisions, faint at its center; induction causes ectopic periclinal divisions and meristem termination

basis: Class III HD-ZIP marking the dorsal domain of the apical meristem (Spencer et al. 2024 Development)
validation: translational proMpC3HDZ:gMpC3HDZ-VENUS restricted to the dorsal surface of the mature meristem; appears 1-2 days after gemma germination

basis: Cellulose synthase-like D needed for rhizoid tip growth; same orthogroup as Arabidopsis root-hair CSLD3 (Honkanen et al. 2016 Curr Biol)
validation: T-DNA mutants form short rhizoids (Fig 1A); no reporter localization

basis: Cellulose synthase-like D needed for rhizoid tip growth (Honkanen et al. 2016 Curr Biol)
validation: T-DNA mutants form short rhizoids (Fig 1A); no reporter localization

basis: U-box E3 ligase required for schizogenous air-chamber formation from dorsal epidermal cells (Ishizaki et al. 2013 Plant Cell)
validation: nop1 mutants form no air chambers, leaving a single-layer dorsal epidermis; NOP1 is plasma-membrane localized; no tissue reporter

basis: Single LRL-class (group XI) bHLH; general growth regulator required for rhizoid development; knockdown also causes epidermal defects, so not rhizoid-specific (Breuninger et al. 2016 Curr Biol). Arabidopsis LRL3 marks root hairs.
validation: Mplrl knockdown/loss of function: reduced rhizoids and general growth defects (Breuninger 2016); IDs from MarpolBase nomenclature (MpLRL: Mapoly0502s0001; Mpzg01410 v5.1; Mp2g20695)
